sample: Regular-season games 2013-2025 with archived closing lines

rows.question: Are the closing spread and closing total of the same game correlated?
rows.note: Tests whether a game's expected margin carries information about its expected pace.
rows.source: computed from data/source/games.csv (nflverse archive) — reproducible via pipeline/correlations.py

rows.question: Are the final margin and final total of the same game correlated?
rows.note: Game-script dependence: blowouts can suppress or inflate totals.
rows.source: computed from data/source/games.csv (nflverse archive) — reproducible via pipeline/correlations.py

rows.question: Within one game, does the favourite covering correlate with the under hitting?
rows.note: This is the dependence a same-game parlay must price. A negative phi means the book's independent multiplication overprices the combo.
rows.source: computed from data/source/games.csv (nflverse archive) — reproducible via pipeline/correlations.py

rows.question: Does the model's disagreement with the closing line predict the actual result?
rows.note: If this is ~0 the model has no exploitable information at closing prices.
rows.source: computed from data/source/games.csv (nflverse archive) — reproducible via pipeline/correlations.py

rows.question: Do two legs of a cross-game parlay on the same week move together?
rows.note: Near zero is expected: independent games. It is the assumption behind multiplying parlay legs.
rows.source: computed from data/source/games.csv (nflverse archive) — reproducible via pipeline/correlations.py

rows.question: Do a quarterback's passing yards and his team's total points correlate in the same game?
rows.note: No authorized 2026 player-level feed and no player game logs are bundled in this workspace. No value is estimated.

rows.question: Do two same-game player prop legs (e.g. QB passing yards + WR1 receiving yards) correlate?
rows.note: Requires player-level data and archived same-game parlay prices. Neither is in scope. No proxy is substituted.

interpretation_guard: Correlation is not causation and not an edge.
All values are DERIVED from a third-party archive, not official NFL statistics.
Confidence intervals are Fisher-z approximations and ignore week clustering; treat them as indicative.
